title: 2.1 Calculating enthalpy changes: calorimetry, Hess's law and bond energies

q.Q1: Q1. Burning 0.46 g of ethanol (Mr 46) heats 200 g of water by 13.0 °C. Calculate Q and the molar enthalpy of combustion (c = 4.2 J/g/°C).

q.Q2: Q2. 50 cm3 of 2 M HCl and 50 cm3 of 2 M NaOH rise from 22.0 °C to 35.5 °C. Calculate the molar enthalpy of neutralisation.
q.Q3: Q3. Why does ethanoic acid give a smaller enthalpy of neutralisation than hydrochloric acid?

q.Q4: Q4. C(s) + O2 → CO2, ΔH = −394 kJ/mol; CO + ½O2 → CO2, ΔH = −283 kJ/mol. Use Hess's law to find ΔH for C + ½O2 → CO.

q.Q5: Q5. Calculate ΔH for H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl. Bond energies: H–H 436, Cl–Cl 242, H–Cl 431 kJ/mol.

q.Q6: Q6. The measured enthalpy of combustion of ethanol is much less than the data-book value (−1367 kJ/mol). Give two reasons and one improvement.
